primitives.name: Ball Delivery Segmentation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our research tries to solve one of these problems by segmenting ball deliveries in a cricket broadcast using deep learning models, MobileNet and YOLO, thus enabling researchers to use our work as a dataset for their research.
primitives.assumptions: Video frames are temporally sequential; ball delivery events are distinct from replays or non-delivery scenes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when background subtraction fails due to camera motion or ball occlusion.

layer2.mapping: Segmentation maps video frames to discrete ball delivery shots via convolutional neural network classification of spatial features.
layer2.telemetry: Frame-level classification accuracy of delivery vs. replay or non-delivery segments.

primitives.name: Video Shot Extraction
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper presents an approach to segment and extract video shots in which only the ball is being delivered.
primitives.assumptions: Continuous video frames form temporally coherent shots; shot boundaries align with ball delivery events.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when camera motion or scene transition lacks clear visual cues.

layer2.mapping: Extracts video shots by detecting abrupt changes in frame content using background subtraction and color difference metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal consistency score of extracted shot sequences.

primitives.name: Ball Tracking and Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Ball tracking in these video shots is also done using a separate RetinaNet model as a sample of the usefulness of the proposed dataset.
primitives.assumptions: Ball trajectory is visible across frames; pitch scale mapping enables depth estimation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Tracking fails when ball is occluded or camera angle shifts beyond calibration range.

layer2.mapping: RetinaNet tracks ball movement in 2D space and classifies delivery type based on landing point and pitch geometry.
layer2.telemetry: Trajectory deviation from expected pitch path and classification confidence scores.

Ball delivery segmentation uses MobileNet and YOLO to classify video frames into delivery/non-delivery categories, leveraging spatial feature extraction. Video shot extraction relies on background subtraction and color-difference metrics to isolate continuous scenes. Ball tracking applies RetinaNet to infer 2D trajectories and classify delivery types (full-pitch, good-length, short-pitch) by mapping observed motion onto a calibrated pitch. Dualities emerge between frame-level classification and shot-level coherence, with failure modes tied to camera motion, occlusion, and scene ambiguity. Temporal consistency is enforced through frame differencing and motion vector validation. The system's robustness depends on accurate pitch-scale mapping and camera calibration to translate 2D observations into meaningful cricket-specific semantics.
